title: Dense Retrieval with FAISS
contents: Dense retrieval encodes queries and documents into continuous vector representations using transformer models. FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) enables efficient nearest-neighbor search over millions of high-dimensional vectors. Common dense encoders include E5, BGE, Contriever, and DPR. The encoded vectors are indexed with structures such as Flat, IVF, or HNSW indexes depending on the trade-off between speed and recall.

title: BM25 Sparse Retrieval
contents: BM25 is a bag-of-words ranking function that scores documents based on term frequency and inverse document frequency. It is the dominant sparse retrieval baseline and is implemented efficiently via inverted indexes. Pyserini provides a Java-backed BM25 implementation that wraps Apache Lucene. BM25 performs well on keyword-heavy queries and is often used as a first-stage retriever in multi-stage pipelines.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
contents: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines a retriever with a generative language model. The retriever fetches relevant documents for a given query, and the generator conditions its output on both the query and the retrieved context. RAG reduces hallucinations and enables the model to access up-to-date knowledge without retraining. Common retrievers in RAG pipelines include BM25, DPR, and E5.

title: Cross-Encoder Reranking
contents: Cross-encoders rerank a short list of candidate documents by jointly encoding the query and each document through a single transformer. Unlike bi-encoders that produce independent query and document embeddings, cross-encoders attend across both inputs simultaneously, producing more accurate relevance scores. They are slower but highly effective as a second-stage reranker. ms-marco-MiniLM is a popular lightweight cross-encoder trained on the MS MARCO passage dataset.

title: Sentence Transformers
contents: Sentence Transformers is a Python library built on top of Hugging Face Transformers that produces dense sentence embeddings. It supports both bi-encoder models for fast semantic search and cross-encoder models for precise reranking. Models are fine-tuned with contrastive loss on sentence pairs. The library integrates directly with FAISS and Elasticsearch for scalable retrieval.

title: E5 Embedding Models
contents: E5 (EmbEddings from bidirEctional Encoder rEpresentations) is a family of text embedding models from Microsoft. E5 models are trained with contrastive learning on large-scale text pairs and require a task prefix such as 'query:' or 'passage:' prepended to the input text. E5-small, E5-base, and E5-large offer different trade-offs between embedding quality and inference speed.

title: BGE Embedding Models
contents: BGE (BAAI General Embedding) is a series of text embedding models from the Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence. BGE models use CLS token pooling and require a task-specific instruction prefix for query encoding. BGE-M3 supports multilingual retrieval across more than 100 languages and combines dense, sparse, and multi-vector retrieval in a single model.

title: Mean Pooling vs CLS Pooling
contents: Transformer-based encoders produce a sequence of hidden states, one per token. To obtain a single sentence embedding, pooling is applied. Mean pooling averages the token hidden states weighted by the attention mask, producing a smooth representation of the entire sequence. CLS pooling uses only the hidden state of the special [CLS] token, which is designed to aggregate sequence-level information. E5 and Contriever use mean pooling; BGE uses CLS pooling.

title: FastAPI for ML Serving
contents: FastAPI is a modern Python web framework for building REST APIs with automatic OpenAPI documentation. It is built on top of Starlette and Pydantic for request validation. FastAPI is commonly used to serve machine learning models because of its async support, high throughput, and concise syntax. Uvicorn is the recommended ASGI server for running FastAPI applications in production.

title: FAISS Index Types
contents: FAISS supports multiple index types suited to different workloads. IndexFlatIP performs exact inner-product search and is the most accurate but slowest for large corpora. IVFFlat partitions the vector space into Voronoi cells and performs approximate search within the nearest cells. HNSWFlat builds a hierarchical navigable small world graph for fast approximate nearest-neighbor search. The choice of index type depends on corpus size, latency budget, and acceptable recall trade-off.

title: Contriever Retrieval Model
contents: Contriever is an unsupervised dense retrieval model trained without labeled query-document pairs. It uses momentum contrastive learning to align representations of semantically similar text spans. Contriever and its multilingual variant mContriever apply mean pooling over the final hidden states. Despite being unsupervised, Contriever achieves competitive retrieval performance on open-domain question answering benchmarks.

title: DPR: Dense Passage Retrieval
contents: Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR) trains separate bi-encoder models for queries and passages using supervised contrastive learning on question-answer pairs. The query encoder and passage encoder are fine-tuned independently on annotated retrieval data such as Natural Questions and TriviaQA. DPR embeddings are not normalized before indexing, distinguishing it from models like E5 and BGE that normalize embeddings to unit length.

title: Google Custom Search API
contents: Google Custom Search JSON API allows developers to programmatically query a Programmable Search Engine (CSE). It returns up to 10 results per request and supports faceted search, safe search filters, and date range restrictions. The API requires a developer key and a CSE identifier. Responses include the page title, URL, and a short snippet extracted from the matching page content.

title: SerpAPI Web Search
contents: SerpAPI is a real-time web scraping API that parses search engine result pages into structured JSON. It supports Google, Bing, Baidu, and other engines. Responses include organic results, answer boxes, knowledge graphs, and related questions. SerpAPI handles JavaScript rendering and CAPTCHA solving transparently. It is commonly used in research pipelines that require live web search results.

title: Vocabulary and Tokenization
contents: Text vocabulary construction involves normalizing tokens by lowercasing, removing punctuation, and stripping diacritics. Each unique token is assigned a sequential integer index. Token frequencies are tracked to support TF-IDF weighting and keyword extraction. Keyword extraction selects the most frequent normalized tokens from a document as its representative terms. These keywords are useful for sparse indexing, BM25 scoring, and query expansion.

title: Multi-Stage Retrieval Pipelines
contents: Multi-stage retrieval pipelines combine a fast first-stage retriever with a slower but more accurate second-stage reranker. The first stage retrieves a large candidate set using BM25 or a bi-encoder. The second stage reranks the candidates using a cross-encoder that scores each query-document pair jointly. This two-stage approach balances recall from the first stage with precision from the reranker.

title: Batch Inference with PyTorch
contents: Batch inference groups multiple inputs together to maximize GPU utilization. Transformer models benefit greatly from batching because matrix multiplications scale efficiently on parallel hardware. DataParallel splits batches across multiple GPUs automatically. Using float16 precision with mixed-precision inference halves memory usage and increases throughput on modern CUDA devices. Tokenizer padding and truncation ensure uniform sequence lengths within a batch.

title: Open-Domain Question Answering
contents: Open-domain question answering (ODQA) requires retrieving relevant passages from a large corpus and then extracting or generating an answer. Standard benchmarks include Natural Questions, TriviaQA, and WebQuestions. The retriever component is typically evaluated by passage recall at k, measuring whether the gold passage appears in the top-k retrieved results. Reader models such as FiD and RAG-Token consume all retrieved passages jointly to produce an answer.

title: MS MARCO Passage Ranking
contents: MS MARCO is a large-scale reading comprehension and passage ranking dataset collected from Bing search logs. The passage ranking task involves scoring a list of candidate passages for a given query. Models are evaluated using MRR@10 and NDCG@10 metrics. MS MARCO has been used to fine-tune cross-encoders such as MiniLM and MonoT5 for reranking, and bi-encoders such as DPR and TAS-B for dense first-stage retrieval.

title: Vector Similarity Search
contents: Vector similarity search finds the nearest neighbors of a query vector in a large collection of stored vectors. Inner product and cosine similarity are the most common distance metrics for text embeddings. Cosine similarity is equivalent to inner product when vectors are normalized to unit length. Approximate nearest-neighbor algorithms such as HNSW and IVF trade a small accuracy loss for significant speedups over exact exhaustive search at large scale.
